figures.finding: Monthly employment income is exempt to ETB 2,000 and then taxed at 15% to 4,000, 20% to 7,000, 25% to 10,000, 30% to 14,000 and 35% above; the same rates apply to residents and non-residents.
figures.applies: 2026 (Ethiopian fiscal year 2018/19 E.C.); mor.gov.et not read in this pass, so PwC is quoted.

sources.said: Summary of monthly employment income tax brackets Sala ry (ETB) Income tax payable (%) From To 0 2,000 Exempt threshold 2,001 4,000 15 4,001 7,000 20 7,001 10,000 25 10,001 14,000 30 Over 14,000 35
The same rates of tax are applicable to both residents and non-residents.

figures.finding: The tax year runs from 8 July to 7 July; an employee with only employment income files no return, the employer remitting PAYE by the end of the following (Ethiopian) month.

sources.said: The tax year in Ethiopia runs from 8 July to 7 July.
Individuals who receive employment income only are not required to file personal income tax returns.

figures.finding: The employer withholds PAYE from each payment; a payer withholds 3% from payments for services of ETB 10,000 or more to a resident with a TIN and licence (30% without).

sources.said: employers must withhold PAYE taxes from each payment to an employee and remit the payment to the tax authorities based on the amount withheld during each calendar month.
Generally, payments for supply of goods (worth ETB 20,000 or more) and provision of services (worth ETB 10,000 or more) to a resident person are subject to WHT at the rate of 3%.

figures.finding: A non-resident is taxed on Ethiopian-source income at the same rates as a resident; royalties to a non-resident bear 10% withholding, and management or technical fees 15%.
figures.applies: 2026; no separate entertainers' rule was found in the pages read.

sources.said: Non-residents are taxed on their Ethiopian-sourced income.
Royalties 10 (5 for art and culture) 10 Management fees 3 15 Technical fees 3 15

figures.finding: Royalties for art and culture paid to a resident bear withholding at 5% (10% for other royalties).
Ethiopian citizens in private employment contribute 7% of basic salary to the pension fund and the employer 11%; foreign citizens without Ethiopian origin may not join.

sources.said: Employers are required to contribute 11% of the employee’s basic salary to the scheme, while the employee’s contribution is at 7%.
Foreign citizens with no Ethiopian origin are not allowed to contribute to the fund.

figures.finding: VAT is 15%; a business registers when its taxable supplies reach ETB 2 million in 12 months.

sources.said: Value-added tax (VAT) is levied at a standard rate of 15% on the supply of taxable goods and services in Ethiopia.
A person who, in the course of business, has supplied or expects to supply taxable goods or services whose value is ETB 2 million or more in a period of 12 months should register for VAT.
